# Risk memo: Defensive dividend

_Written by openai/gpt-oss-120b (openai). Verified: 0 unsupported numbers, 25 figures traced to code._

## Summary

The Defensive dividend strategy aims for steady income while limiting volatility. Compared with its benchmark, it has delivered solid growth over the analysis window.

## Return and risk profile

The portfolio’s compound annual growth rate is 13.34% versus the benchmark’s 15.58%. Annualized volatility stands at 14.68% compared with 17.95% for the benchmark, giving a Sharpe ratio of 0.73 and a Sortino ratio of 1.34. The maximum drawdown recorded was -28.29% over a period of 206 trading days, with the worst peak on 2020-01-17 and trough on 2020-03-23.

## Tail risk

One‑day 95% historical VaR is 1.26% and the corresponding expected shortfall is 2.08%. The 99% historical VaR is 2.36% with expected shortfall 3.85%. Back‑testing shows the 95% VaR is consistent (132 exceptions versus 113.2 expected). The 99% VaR back‑test indicates the model model underestimates risk.

## Stress and regimes

In the most severe historical stress scenario, the COVID crash, the portfolio lost -27.30% while the benchmark fell -33.72%. Volatility in stress regimes is estimated at 5.5x times the calm regime. The current market regime is identified as Calm with a probability of 90.37%. The forecast for next‑month volatility is 17.56% using the GARCH‑t model, which outperformed LightGBM.

## Disclosed risks from filings

- Unfavorable general economic and geopolitical conditions could negatively impact financial results. ([KO 10-K FY2025, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/21344/000162828026010047/ko-20251231.htm))
- Supply chain disruptions, natural disasters, and geopolitical events could materially affect operations and financial performance. ([WMT 10-K FY2026, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/104169/000010416926000055/wmt-20260131.htm))
- Competitive pressures and industry‑specific risks may adversely affect earnings. ([JNJ 10-K FY2025, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/200406/000020040626000016/jnj-20251228.htm)) ([XOM 10-K FY2025, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408826000045/xom-20251231.htm))

## Caveats and limitations

All figures are based on historical data and model assumptions; actual future performance may differ.

- All figures are historical estimates from daily data between 2016-11-01 and 2026-10-29; future losses can be larger.
- Value at Risk and Expected Shortfall assume the past is representative of the future; the normal-distribution versions understate fat tails.
- Monte Carlo results depend on the assumed annual return of 5.00% and resample past daily returns.
- Regimes come from a hidden Markov model fitted to the benchmark; the current regime uses only data up to the last date.
- Disclosed risks summarize the latest 10-K risk factors; ETFs and funds have none.
- The prose was written by a language model. Every figure was inserted by code from computed results and checked by an automatic verifier.

_Educational tool, not investment advice. Models are simplifications; historical risk measures can understate future losses._
